To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of PEO-PPO-PEOsulfolane system can be used to prepare PVDF/P123 blend microporous membrane with high ionic conductivity and good mechanical properties.
the P123 weight ratio and cooling rate have some effect on the porous structure and mechanical property of PVDF/P123 blend membranes prepared via TIPS process.
the addition of PEO-PPO-PEOs (P123) to PVDF/sulfolane solution can decrease the dynamic crystallization temperatures of the system, which is beneficial for the formation of PVDF microporous membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of P123 on the properties of PVDF/P123 blend microporous membrane prepared by thermally induced phase-separation process.
the preparation of PVDF/P123 blend microporous membrane via TIPS process.
the effects of the change in crystallinity, porous morphology, etc. on the properties of PVDF/P123 blend membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of P123 would not change the crystallization process of PVDF but would change the phase diagram, crystallinity, porous morphology, thermal stability and mechanical properties of the resulting membranes.
the addition of P123 could improve the mechanical properties and thermal stability of the resulting PVDF membranes.

P123 can be used as a good pore former for the preparation of PVDF membranes via TIPS process, and the cooling rate and P123 weight fraction have some influence on the porous structure and mechanical property of the membranes, but have little influence on the polymer crystallinity and thermal stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TIPS process was an efficient way to fabricate PVDF/P123 blend microporous membrane, which could be used as a separator in the lithium ion battery.
the P123 weight fractions and the cooling rate had some effect on the morphology and properties of the PVDF/ P123 blend membranes.
the P123 weight ratio and the cooling rate have some influence on the morphology, crystallinity and porous structure, and thus on the mechanical properties of the PVDF membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TIPS process is suitable to prepare PVDF/ P123 blend microporous membrane with good performance for application in lithium ion battery.
the addition of P123 could improve the mechanical properties and thermal stability of the membranes.
the addition of P123 to the PVDF/sulfolane solution could improve the ionic conductivity and thermal stability of the resulting membranes.
